- Small, densely packed orange-brown pustules
- Appears primarily on the upper leaf surface
- No black pustules visible (ruling out mature Common rust)

Top candidates: **Southern_rust** or **Common_rust**. Let me check reference images.

The Southern rust reference (bottom-right panel) closely matches the test image: dense, small orange-brown pustules on the upper leaf surface with tan tissue damage areas. Let me also check Physoderma brown spot to rule it out.
Physoderma and Gray leaf spot are clearly different. I've confirmed the dense orange pustules. Let me view one more reference to round out my budget.

Tar spot shows black raised spots — clearly different from the orange pustules in the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

| Feature | Test Image | Southern rust | Common rust |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pustule color | Orange-brown | Orange to cinnamon-red ✓ | Golden-brown to cinnamon |
| Pustule size | Small, dense | Small, densely packed ✓ | Larger, more elongated |
| Surface | Primarily upper | Almost exclusively upper ✓ | Both surfaces |
| Tissue damage | Tan areas | Present in severe cases ✓ | Can occur |

The test image matches **Southern rust** — small, densely packed orange-brown pustules concentrated on the upper leaf surface, with associated tan necrotic tissue. The bottom-right panel of the Southern rust collage is nearly identical.
